summary: Brick light on Round Island in the Straits of Mackinac, first shown 15 May 1896, off service from 1947, now solar-powered and run by the Forest Service.

corrections.why: The Board's report for the year ended 30 June 1896 records the light established on 15 May 1896; the Forest Service says commissioned 15 May 1896. The 1895 date is the year of construction and the USLHS lens date (1895).

corrections.proposed: square brick tower forming the northeast corner of the keepers' dwelling
corrections.why: The 1896 report describes 'a square brick tower at one corner'; LighthouseFriends and USLHS (Tower Shape: SQUARE) agree.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Service, the Society and USLHS date the end of service to 1947 (USLHS also gives 'Year Discontinued: 1947-1996'); LighthouseFriends says decommissioned 1955. The light is today an active aid with a solar optic, so the record should not say 'discontinued' without a date for its return.

The Forest Service and the Society say automated in 1924; LighthouseFriends says it became unattended in 1948. Both can be true (automation first, unattended after the Passage light), but the sources do not say so explicitly.
LighthouseFriends: 51 ft; USLHS: 45 ft to the lantern. The story uses LighthouseFriends' figure with the note.
LighthouseFriends: August 1974; the Society's history: 3 July 1978. The record has 1974-08-21.

resolved_conflicts.field: keeper George W. Smith's end date
resolved_conflicts.explanation: USLHS roster gives 1911-1924. LighthouseFriends' keeper list gives 1911-1922, the year of the whisky-still reprimand after which both keepers were transferred. The story states both dates.

USLHS record: 'Year Discontinued: 1947-1996' and 'Private Aid: No'. LighthouseFriends: commenced operation as a private navigational aid in 1996. The Society: lighthouse 'being reactivated' in 1996. The story gives 1996 with both sources.

notes_for_editor: Same name, different place: the LHB reports and the Commissioner volumes also name a 'Round Island' in the St. Marys River (Sault Ste. Marie) and one off Pascagoula, Mississippi. Those are excluded, as are Bulletin index entries for keepers named 'Round Island' (Harry Brouwer, Tony Ryan, F. A. Schreiber) whose station could not be tied to the Straits. The 1914 gale rescue, the 1922 reprimand, the 1914 characteristic change and the 1928 diaphone come from LighthouseFriends only; the Bulletins I searched did not confirm them. The NRHP nomination for 74000994 is not digitised (NPGallery placeholder), so the nomination was not read. The roster is 30 lines from the USLHS record; William Marshall's name is printed 'William Marshall II' there and 'William Marshall' elsewhere. The USLHS record gives 'Year Original Lens Installed: 1895', which may be the lens delivery date; not used in the story. Current characteristic in the record (Fl(2) W 10s, ENC) is not confirmed by any source read. The brief dates this batch 2026-10-22; the system date was 2026-10-27, which is the accessed date used. Fact-check 2026-10-22: removed the sentence saying no source gives a relight date (LighthouseFriends and the Society both date 1996). Removed the attribution of the 1948 Round Island Passage opening to the Coast Guard (LighthouseFriends does not name the operator). The Forest Service 'please call' sentence is about learning more, not visiting; the story now says so. The 1896 whistle entry ('established October 20, 1896') is in the FY1897 report, scan 428, not FY1896. The 1914 rescue and the 1922 reprimand remain LighthouseFriends-only; the Bulletin search did not show them, so the story attributes both to LighthouseFriends.
